[EFFECT]
The year feature has a clear, monotonically rising effect on predicted hourly demand: hours in 2011 receive a negative contribution (reducing predicted rentals by roughly 20%), while hours in 2012 receive a positive contribution (boosting predicted rentals by roughly 23%). Overall, the model estimates that demand in 2012 was around 50% higher than in 2011 for comparable hours. The effect acts essentially as a step change between the two years, with no complex intermediate shape.

[IMPORTANCE]
Year is the 3rd most important feature out of 9, with an importance score of 0.217 — making it a major driver of predicted demand, behind only a couple of other features. Its influence is substantial enough that ignoring year-over-year growth could significantly skew demand forecasts.

[RECOMMENDATION]
Since ridership grew strongly between 2011 and 2012, planners should build in an explicit year-over-year growth factor when projecting future bike and staff requirements, rather than assuming demand stays constant from one year to the next.
